request: Let me mark important tasks and focus on those first

questions.ask: Is 'important' a simple on/off star for each task, or do you want levels like High / Medium / Low?
questions.why: On/off gives one star button per task and one sort rule. Levels need a picker on every task, three-way sorting, and a choice about what a brand-new task defaults to.

questions.ask: Should important tasks always jump to the top of the one list automatically, or should the list stay in its current order with a 'show only important' switch you turn on when you want to focus?
questions.why: Auto-sort changes the order of the list you see every time. A switch leaves the list alone and adds a filter control. These are different screens and different work.

questions.ask: Once you tick an important task as done, should it stay pinned at the top or drop below the tasks still to do?
questions.why: Decides whether completed items keep occupying the focus area at the top, and whether 'done' or 'important' wins when sorting.

answers.ask: Is 'important' a simple on/off star for each task, or do you want levels like High / Medium / Low?
answers.why: On/off gives one star button per task and one sort rule. Levels need a picker on every task, three-way sorting, and a choice about what a brand-new task defaults to.
answers.answer: Just on and off. Important or Normal.

answers.ask: Should important tasks always jump to the top of the one list automatically, or should the list stay in its current order with a 'show only important' switch you turn on when you want to focus?
answers.why: Auto-sort changes the order of the list you see every time. A switch leaves the list alone and adds a filter control. These are different screens and different work.
answers.answer: A separate view. Keep the current order.

answers.ask: Once you tick an important task as done, should it stay pinned at the top or drop below the tasks still to do?
answers.why: Decides whether completed items keep occupying the focus area at the top, and whether 'done' or 'important' wins when sorting.
answers.answer: Completion and ordering should not change at all.

spec.summary: Add an on/off important flag per task, plus a filter view that shows only important tasks without changing list order.
acceptance: Each task in the list has an important control that toggles between Important and Normal.
Toggling a task's important state persists across a page reload.
A newly added task starts as Normal.
A control on the page switches between showing all tasks and showing only important tasks.
With the important-only view on, the list shows every important task and no normal task.
With the important-only view on, the visible important tasks appear in the same relative order as in the all-tasks view.
Switching the important-only view off restores the full list in its original order.
Important tasks are visually distinguishable from normal tasks in the all-tasks view.
GET /api/tasks returns the important state for each task.
PATCH /api/tasks/:id accepts an important boolean and returns the updated task.
unchanged: Tasks stay ordered by id in the all-tasks view; important tasks do not move to the top.
Marking a task done or not done works as before and persists across reload.
Completing a task does not move it in the list and does not change its important state.
Toggling important does not change a task's done state.
Adding a task appends it at the end of the list as before.
Seeded tasks Task A, Task B, and Renew the domain remain listed with their existing done states.
POST /api/tasks with an empty title still returns 400, and PATCH on an unknown id still returns 404.
spec.check: An automated browser check must prove: toggling a task to important persists across reload; turning on the important-only view shows exactly the important tasks in their original relative order; turning it off restores the full list in id order; and completing a task changes neither list position nor important state.
